safety.en: Quieter roads felt comfortable, but this is still roadside running. The larger road and limited space in places needed more attention.

scenery.en: A calm mix of fields, rolling hills and small Monferrato villages. A different kind of enjoyment from the dramatic views in Chianti.

surface.en: Mostly asphalt, with some patched and rougher sections on the country roads.

access.en: A useful mix of gentler hills and a flatter middle section. The full 32.8 km and the uphill return still need planning.

experience.en: A very enjoyable long run with a quieter rural atmosphere and a memorable plate of truffle pasta afterwards.

en.title: Mombaruzzo towards Cantalupo
en.excerpt: A gentler 32.8 km long-run loop through Monferrato, with rolling hills, a flatter middle, an uphill return and epic truffle pasta.
en.body:
After the steep hills and heat of [my Tuscany long run](/journal/tuscany-chianti/), Mombaruzzo felt like a gentler option for a long loop. There were still climbs and descents, but the landscape flowed more easily. For any Estonian readers, the rolling hills reminded me a little of Otepää: mostly gentler rises and dips, with the occasional steeper bit if you go looking for it.

Mombaruzzo is in Piedmont’s Monferrato countryside, south-west of Milan. It is [roughly an hour and a half by car from Milan](https://www.rome2rio.com/s/Mombaruzzo/Milan), depending on where you leave from and the traffic. This was a much quieter setting for a run, with fields on either side, small villages and air that felt fresh.

![Mombaruzzo above fields and vineyards in green Monferrato countryside](/assets/places/mombaruzzo.jpg "Mombaruzzo and its surrounding countryside. Photo: [Alessandro Vecchi](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Mombaruzzo_panorama.jpg) · [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0).")

## The loop: 32.8 km, with a flatter middle

The full loop was 32.8 km, with approximately 350 m of climbing according to the GPX. It heads out through Bruno and towards the Carentino area, continues north-east towards the roads below Cantalupo, then turns back through Borgoratto Alessandrino and the Gamalero side before returning to Mombaruzzo.

The northern end stays south of Cantalupo’s centre, which is why I describe the run as heading towards Cantalupo. It is a full loop with a different way back, rather than a run into the village followed by the same road home.

There is a fairly sustained descent on the way from Mombaruzzo towards Bruno in the opening few kilometres. Around 7 to 8 km, on the approach to the Carentino area, the road rises from roughly 120 to 165 m. That is one of the more noticeable early climbs, but it is a much smaller block than the long climbs in Chianti.

The lowest and flattest part comes farther north, broadly between 12 and 20 km, on the approach towards Cantalupo and the return through Borgoratto Alessandrino. Much of that section sits around 100 to 120 m. It is the part of the profile that offers the longest break from climbing.

On the Gamalero side, around 20 to 26 km, the road gradually rises again with some small changes in gradient. There is another drop after that, followed by more rolling ground. The final few kilometres back towards Mombaruzzo bring a proper uphill return, climbing from around 160 m to roughly 300 m before easing into the village. That is the part I would keep some energy for.

![Elevation profile of the 32.8 km Mombaruzzo loop, with Bruno, the Carentino area, Borgoratto, Gamalero and the return towards Mombaruzzo labelled approximately](/assets/uploads/mombaruzzo-cantalupo/elevation-profile.svg "32.8 km for the full loop and about 350 m of climbing. Place labels are approximate; small elevation fluctuations are smoothed.")

## Quiet roads, with a few busier stretches

There was less traffic in Mombaruzzo itself, and even while running beside the road I did not feel particularly unsafe. I liked the quiet countryside and the feeling of moving between little villages rather than constantly negotiating a busy city.

This is still roadside running. A dedicated riverside running path gives you a different level of separation from cars, and I would not give these roads the same safety score. The loop also includes a larger road on the Gamalero side, where I needed to be more attentive than on the quieter lanes. Bends and limited roadside space still deserve attention, however peaceful the surroundings look.

For me, the combination worked well: manageable hills, open fields and enough quieter stretches to enjoy a long run. It felt considerably less punishing than the particular loop I ran in Tuscany.

## And then, truffle pasta

This is Italy, so the food has to make an appearance. I ate at a small restaurant in Mombaruzzo, and the truffle pasta was epic. I really like that flavour, and this was one of those meals that became part of the memory of the place.

Truffles are part of the local food culture: there are even [truffle grounds and organised hunts in Mombaruzzo](https://www.agriturismobastian.it/farm-holidays-in-monferrato/truffle-hunting-at-mombaruzzo.php).

![A plate of pasta topped with generous truffle shavings at a restaurant in Mombaruzzo](/assets/uploads/mombaruzzo-cantalupo/truffle-pasta.jpg "The truffle pasta in Mombaruzzo. A very good reason to make time for food as well as running.")
